subject: Post-call: model fit & tool-calling evals / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sam Carter <sam@averyanalytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-05T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: model fit & tool-calling evals / next steps

Hi Sam — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap
- Goal: automate structured extraction and action triggering from customer support transcripts (JSON schema outputs + function/tool calling into Avery's internal ticket system).
- Key constraints: 200–400 token average context, 1–2 second P95 latency target for real-time routing, and strict schema compliance for downstream automation.

Model-fit / eval highlights we discussed
- Early bench: RW-Instruct-13B (balanced) and RW-Optima-7B (low-latency) gave highest F1 on entity extraction.
- Structured-output eval (our test harness w/ your sample set): ~92% JSON schema compliance across schemas (main failures were nested arrays with numeric formatting for price fields and occasional missing keys when responses truncated).
- Tool-calling checks: retries and idempotency surfaced as primary sources of nondeterminism; we observed a small number of duplicate calls when client retry logic lacked idempotency tokens.

Attachments we shared in this thread: a short model-fit report and the prompt sets we used for the run (see attached: avery_model_fit_eval_v1.pdf, avery_eval_prompt_sets_v1.json, prompt_sets.zip).

Recommended next steps (proposed timeline)
1) Run a 5k-sample eval using your redacted dataset (we can host the run in a sandbox) — deliverable: per-schema compliance report + failure cases (3 business days).
2) Technical deep-dive (30–45m) with Aditya on runtime config and retry/backoff patterns (we think a simple exponential backoff with jitter + idempotency tokens solves most duplicate-tool-call issues). Can you do Wed or Thu next week?
3) If results look good, pilot with RW-Instruct-13B quantized profile (balanced-latency) behind Redwood-Dedicated for 2 weeks to validate production throughput.

Short asks for you
- Share preferred Wed/Thu times for the deep-dive and a sample of 5k redacted transcripts (s3 link or shared Drive).
- Confirm team contact for infra questions (loop in Lena if that's correct).

Bench & docs (quick refs)
- Model fit dashboard: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/avery-eval-report
- Structured-output best practices: https://docs.redwood.com/guides/structured-output

Thanks — looking forward.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0142

Sam / Lena — great, Wed 1:30pm PT works on our side. I've penciled it with Aditya and Rishi. Calendar invite to follow.

Answers to the two asks from call and your note: 

1) Quantization guidance & quality delta- Recommended path: RW-Instruct-13B with Q4_K_M (4-bit mixed block quantization) profile from Redwood Optimize set to "balanced-latency". In our benchmark runs on your data shape we observed:
   - FP16 baseline -> Q4_K_M: median token-latency down ~40–55% and throughput up ~1.8x.
   - Quality: entity extraction F1 dropped ~0.8–1.5 points on average on our eval set; structured-output schema compliance was largely unaffected for non-truncated responses.
   - If you need <0.5 pt quality delta, run the pilot on Dedicated capacity and we can increase context cache and token budget.

2) Retries & idempotency- Concrete recommendation: include an idempotency-token header (UUID v4) on every tool/function call originating from the LLM output. Server-side (Avery ticket service) should reject duplicates with 409 when the token is seen and return the canonical resource id. Client-side retry policy: exponential backoff with jitter (base=100ms, factor=2, max=2s, attempts=5). For async tool calls consider callback webhook with same token so duplicate calls are harmless. Aditya will walk through sample code in the deep-dive.

3) JSON schema compliance improvements we can apply before pilot
   - Use Redwood structured-output validator in the generation loop (we run the model -> validate -> if invalid, retry with schema hinting up to 2 attempts). This raised compliance from ~92% -> ~97% in our internal tests.
   - For numeric formatting issues (price, quantity) add a small post-processing step that enforces types before commit.

I've re-attached the prompt sets and a short runbook for retries (prompt_sets.zip, avery_eval_prompt_sets_v1.json). Also linking the run results and a concise playbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/avery-eval-report and https://redwood.hubspot.com/deal/HW-2027-0042

Next actions from us
- We'll queue the 5k eval as soon as you drop the data link — expect results in ~72 hours.
- Aditya will present retry/backoff + example idempotency code in Wed's meeting.

If Lena or your infra team want a separate session on API contracts, we can do that the following week.

Thanks — see you Wed at 1:30pm PT.

Best,
Marissa Cole
